cues.en: So let's play around with item-based collaborative filtering.
cues.zh: 來實驗項目式協同過濾。

cues.en: Open Spyder back up, and take a look at SimpleItemCF.py.
cues.zh: 重新開啟 Spyder，看看 SimpleItemCF.py。

cues.en: As you might expect, it looks a lot like SimpleUserCF.py, because the general approach is the same as user-based collaborative filtering, we're just focusing on relationships
cues.zh: 如你所料，它很像 SimpleUserCF.py，因為一般方法與使用者式協同過濾相同，只是專注在

cues.en: between items instead of users.
cues.zh: 項目而不是使用者之間的關係。

cues.en: The first difference you'll see is that when we set up the sim_options, we're passing false for; 'user based.'
cues.zh: 第一個差異是，設定 sim_options 時，對 user_based 傳入 False。

cues.en: This tells the surprise library to generate an item-to-item similarity matrix, using cosine as its similarity metric, instead of a user-to-user similarity matrix.
cues.zh: 這會告訴 Surprise 函式庫，以餘弦作為相似度指標，產生項目間相似度矩陣，而不是使用者間相似度矩陣。

cues.en: Next we pull of the top-K highest rated items for our test user, and then we look up all of the items similar to each of those items.
cues.zh: 接著，取出測試使用者評分最高的前 k 個項目，再查詢與每個項目相似的所有項目。

cues.en: These become our recommendation candidates, and as we build up our list of candidates, we score them by their similarity score to the item our user rated, and by the rating our user gave that item.
cues.zh: 這些就是推薦候選；建立候選清單時，根據它與使用者評分項目的相似度，以及使用者給該項目的評分，替它計分。

cues.en: The rest of the code is the same, we build up a dictionary of stuff our user has already seen, and while we're printing out the top-scoring results, we filter those out from the final results.
cues.zh: 其餘程式碼相同：建立使用者已看過項目的字典，在印出最高分結果時，將它們從最終結果中排除。

cues.en: If you're new to Python, it's probably a good idea to pause here for a bit and study this code a little more closely.
cues.zh: 如果你是 Python 新手，或許應該在這裡暫停，仔細研究程式碼。

cues.en: But once it's sunk in - let's run it and see what happens!
cues.zh: 理解之後，就執行看看。

cues.en: This too didn't take too long, but the results are interesting.
cues.zh: 這次也沒花太久，但結果很有意思。

cues.en: We're getting much more obscure recommendations than we did with user-based collaborative filtering.
cues.zh: 比使用者式協同過濾，得到更多冷門推薦。

cues.en: However, these were probably really good recommendations for user number 85, whose ratings all date back to the late 1990's.
cues.zh: 不過，這些也許非常適合使用者 85，因為他的評分都可以追溯到 1990 年代末。

cues.en: Because all we know is the movies he liked from 20 years or more ago, we're picking up items similar to those older movies, and those tend to be older movies, as well.
cues.zh: 我們只知道他二十多年前喜歡的電影，因此找出與那些舊電影相似的項目，而它們通常也是舊電影。

cues.en: So there's a bit of bias in the data here that's coloring our results to some extent.
cues.zh: 所以，這裡的資料偏差，在某種程度上影響了結果。

cues.en: It's a good cautionary tale, you can use tools like this to sample the recommendations an algorithm will give you, but you have to be careful when judging these results subjectively.
cues.zh: 這是很好的提醒：可以用這種工具抽看演算法的推薦，但主觀判斷結果時，要很小心。

cues.en: As much as I may have similar tastes to user number 85, I'm not him, and I'm not even in the same time he was in when he left his ratings.
cues.zh: 儘管我可能和使用者 85 品味相似，但我不是他，甚至也不處於他留下評分時的年代。

cues.en: Remember item-based collaborative filtering is what Amazon used with outstanding success, so if you were to prematurely discard this algorithm because its results on one test user
cues.zh: 記得，項目式協同過濾是 Amazon 使用並大獲成功的方法，因此如果只因為它對一位測試使用者的結果

cues.en: didn't resonate with you, that would be a big loss.
cues.zh: 沒有讓你產生共鳴，就過早捨棄這個演算法，會是很大的損失。

cues.en: You need to test it out on several real people if possible, and then move to a large scale A/B test to see if this algorithm really is better or worse than whatever you might have today.
cues.zh: 如果可能，需要在多位真實使用者身上測試，再做大規模 A/B 測試，確認這個演算法，究竟比目前的方法更好還是更差。
